definition: Transitory means lasting only a short time; not permanent.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word transitory. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know transitory should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The raise gave morale only a transitory lift; by spring the old grumbling was back.
Impermanent states only that a thing will not last forever; transitory adds that it is already moving through, a phase on its way out.
Vanishing goes past transitory — dissolving even as you name it, with no season of passage at all.

Passing suits what drifts by of its own accord — a passing mood, a passing fad, a passing shower. It is the light, everyday word. Transitory makes the same promise in a more formal register and suits whole phases and conditions; both leave the leaving to the thing itself.

Short-term means planned to be brief: a stretch someone set on purpose, usually with an end date in writing — a short-term lease, a short-term loan. Transitory carries no plan at all; a transitory state simply passes of its own nature, in its own time.

hunger, the noon crash — every bit of it is transitory, burning off as the body's clock slides into the new zone at roughly a sunrise per day.
Travelers who understand this simply wait it out; the condition was never built to last, and in three mornings it is gone.
Transitory is the exact word because it names what lasts only a short time and is not permanent — a state already on its way out.
It does not demand speed: a transitory phase may take a season to pass.
The word's quiet comfort, and its quiet warning, are the same sentence: it will not stay.
Transitory denies permanence without insisting on speed — it suits phases and conditions that will pass in their own time.
Its cluster-mates in this unit go further: ephemeral squeezes a whole life into a day, and momentary into an instant.
For an arrangement with a posted end date, plain temporary is the businesslike choice.

Every January, when the lake ice thickens past a meter, the county opens the winter road to the island villages.
For eight or nine weeks, trucks deliver a year's worth of fuel, lumber, and flour across water that is, for the season, as solid as any highway.
Everyone involved understands that the road is transitory.
It is a phase of the lake, not a structure on it, and it begins dying from the first warm afternoon.
By late March the heaviest loads are turned away; by April the route is water again, and no sign remains that a road was ever there.
The villages plan around this rhythm, ordering in bulk while the phase lasts and trusting the lake to repeat itself next winter.
